title: Elio's Best Shortcut
markdown:
It was a time in the Northwind Heights, near the wood where the leaves sang like little bells, when the moon was high and the stars looked like shiny stars spilled on the dark sky.

Elio was a young elf. His hair was the colour of autumn leaves, and his eyes were as bright as a robin’s. Today Elio was very excited. He was going to visit his Grandmother Elara. She lived in the village just over the Whispering Hills. Grandmother Elara made the best Moonberry Pie. The crust was golden and flaky. The berries inside sparkled like little jewels. They were sweet and tangy.

Elio had a little pet named Sparkle. Sparkle was a tiny glow-worm, fluffy and soft. When Sparkle wiggled, he glowed with a warm gentle light. He was like a little sunbeam. Sparkle was nestled in a little mossy pouch. Elio wore it around his neck. Sparkle’s little antennae would twitch and wiggle with curiosity at everything Elio saw.

Elio wanted to go the fastest way to Grandmother Elara’s. He knew a shortcut. It was a secret path through the Tinkling Pinewood. But there was a little puzzle. The Tinkling Pinewood was not just any wood. The trees there had leaves that chimed like tiny bells when the breeze tickled them. And the air itself seemed to hum with gentle magic.

Two very clever folk lived near the pinewood. Wizard Fizzwick and Witch Willow. They were having a friendly disagreement. It was a very important disagreement about the very best way to travel.

Wizard Fizzwick had a beard as long as a waterfall. His hat sometimes twinkled with little star-like lights. He loved speed. “The fastest way is always best,” he would say. He would flick his wrist with a puff of sparkly dust from his sleeve. He believed that every moment spent dawdling was a moment lost. A precious chance for adventure or a quick cup of tea.

And Witch Willow, with hair like woven moonbeams, seemed to catch the soft glow of the night sky. She preferred a gentler path. “A winding way, with lovely sights, is far more delightful,” she would chime. Her voice was like the tinkling of wind chimes. She believed the journey itself was just as important as the destination, filled with little wonders to discover.

They stood at the edge of the pinewood. Their noses almost touched. Each pointed to their own favourite path.

“My shortcut is by far the quickest, Elio.” Wizard Fizzwick’s beard practically vibrated with certainty. “A few zippy spells, and poof. You are there. No time for dawdling, no sir.” He imagined Elio arriving fresh as a daisy, with time for an extra story before supper.

“Oh, but Fizzwick.” Willow giggled. Her eyes twinkled like fireflies in the twilight. “My path is much more peaceful. It meanders, you see. Like a happy little stream finding its way to the sea. You will see the shyest forest flowers. You will hear the secret songs of the birds.” She pictured Elio stopping to admire a particularly shiny beetle or a particularly pretty mushroom.

Elio looked from one to the other. Sparkle, nestled in his pouch, gave a little wiggle. His light flickered a tiny bit faster. A nervous flutter. A bit of a puzzle. Elio really wanted to see Grandmother Elara. He wanted to taste that wonderful pie. He knew Grandmother Elara would be waiting for him. Her apron would be dusted with flour. Her oven would be warm and ready. He wanted to get there before the sun peeked over the hills. He wanted to get there before the sky turned rosy.

“Hmm.” Elio stroked his chin. His brow furrowed just a little. He could feel the excitement of the trip. But also a little worry about choosing the right path.

“Let me show you my way.” Fizzwick declared it with a grand flourish. With a wave of his hand, the path before him shimmered. Little bursts of fizzy magic popped like tiny bubbles of light. Elio stepped forward. Suddenly he felt as if he were on a very bouncy trampoline. Boing. Boing. The trees seemed to blur into streaks of green and brown. The air buzzed with happy speedy energy. Sparkle, in his pouch, let out a tiny surprised sneeze. A little puff of light escaped his nose.

“Oh dear.” Elio tried to keep his feet on the ground. “It is very bouncy. My tummy feels like it is doing somersaults.” He tried to imagine Sparkle bouncing along. He felt a pang of worry for his little friend.

Then it was Witch Willow’s turn. “Now, watch this.” A mischievous glint was in her eye. The path in front of her began to weave and curve. It was like a ribbon dancing in the wind. It twisted and turned around ancient mossy trees. It went under low-hanging branches with dew-kissed leaves. It went through little sunlit glades where butterflies flitted. Elio followed her. The path was so winding that he felt a little dizzy. His head spun like a top. Sparkle’s light wobbled precariously.

“My, my.” Elio rubbed his temples. “It is very twisty. I feel as if I am going around in circles.” He imagined himself never quite getting to Grandmother Elara’s. He imagined just looping around and around the same patch of ferns.

Wizard Fizzwick and Witch Willow looked at each other. Their friendly disagreement bubbled up again. “See?” said Fizzwick. He puffed out his chest. “Too much wobbling. Elio needs to be speedy.”

“And yours is too much bouncing.” Willow replied. A friendly smile was on her face, though she did give a little shake of her head. “He could get the hiccups from all that jolting.” They were not truly cross. They just both wanted to help Elio reach his grandmother’s house the very best way they knew how.

And then they heard a big sigh. It sounded like the wind rustling through a field of dry leaves. Coming around a large mossy rock, its surface covered in soft green velvet, was Ogre Grumbler. Now, Grumbler was a very big ogre. His voice was like a rumble of thunder. But he was as gentle as a fluffy cloud. He had kind sleepy eyes. He had big clumsy feet that always seemed a little tired. He just loved a good nap. He was trying to find the quickest way to his favourite sunny spot. The moss there was extra soft. He wanted a much-needed snooze.

“Oh, hello Grumbler.” Willow’s voice was warm and welcoming.

“What is all the fuss?” Grumbler blinked his sleepy eyes. They were the colour of warm honey. He stretched out a big lumpy arm.

“We cannot agree on the best shortcut.” Elio’s voice was a little worried. “Wizard Fizzwick says his way is fastest. And Witch Willow says her way is best.”

Grumbler yawned a giant yawn. It revealed a row of surprisingly small white teeth. “Shortcuts. I just want a shortcut to my nap. My feet are tired.” He sat down with a gentle thud on a patch of clover. The ground vibrated ever so slightly. He patted the soft moss beside him.

Elio looked at Fizzwick’s path. It still shimmered with tempting speed. Then he looked at Willow’s path. It was so pretty and green. But oh, so twisty. And then he looked at Grumbler. He looked quite comfy and peaceful sitting there. A gentle giant in a world that sometimes felt a bit too busy. An idea, like a little golden firefly, sparked in Elio’s mind. He remembered how much he loved his grandmother’s hugs. He remembered how nice it was to feel safe and warm.

“Wait. What if we put our shortcuts together?”

Wizard Fizzwick blinked his sparkly eyes. Witch Willow tilted her head. A curious smile played on her lips. “Together?” The question sounded like a soft melody.

“Yes.” Elio’s excitement grew. “We can use Fizzwick’s speed to get us quickly through the straight parts. The parts that are easy and quick. And then, when the path gets tricky, we can use Willow’s gentle winding way to guide us around the tricky bits. Like fallen logs or prickly bushes. And maybe a nice comfy spot in the middle for a little rest? So Sparkle does not get too bouncy or too dizzy?”

Grumbler’s sleepy eyes lit up a little. A rumble of happiness started deep in his chest. “Rest? And pie?” he added, as an afterthought.

So Wizard Fizzwick, with a cheerful nod, waved his hand. The path ahead zipped with a gentle speedy magic. Elio, with Sparkle snug and safe in his pouch, Willow, with her moonbeam hair catching the light, and Grumbler, with his happy sigh, followed. They moved swiftly but smoothly. When the path started to twist and turn, Witch Willow would hum a little tune, a melody that smelled of lavender and sunshine. And the path would weave around fallen logs and blooming flowers, just as she had promised. And when they needed a moment, Grumbler, with his surprising gentleness, would find a soft patch of moss. They would all have a quick cozy rest. A moment to catch their breath and share a giggle. Sparkle, no longer nervous, glowed with a steady happy light. Elio felt a little pang of worry for Sparkle, but he remembered his promise. He decided that making sure Sparkle was comfortable was more important than being the very fastest.

The path was perfect. It was fast and gentle. They laughed as they travelled, their worries all melted away, like snowflakes on a warm hand. The leaves chimed like tiny bells above them, a soft sweet melody. The mossy ground felt springy beneath their feet. The air smelled like fresh pine needles and sweet berries. The leaves tinkled around them, and the air hummed with their shared joy.

As they reached the edge of the pinewood, the sky was turning a soft pink and orange. The sun was just beginning to wake up. It painted the clouds with streaks of gold and rose. And there, waiting by her little cottage with a wide welcoming smile, was Grandmother Elara. Her apron was dusted with flour. A table was set with a beautiful steaming Moonberry Pie. The aroma of sweet berries and warm pastry wafted towards them.

Ogre Grumbler’s sleepy eyes widened. A happy rumble escaped him. “Pie?”

Grandmother Elara chuckled. Her eyes crinkled at the corners. “Come in, come in, all of you. There is plenty for everyone. And I have a special spot just for you, Grumbler, where the sun is extra warm.”

And so Elio, Sparkle, Wizard Fizzwick, Witch Willow, and Ogre Grumbler sat together. They shared the delicious Moonberry Pie. The pie was warm and sweet. And the company was even sweeter. Grumbler, full of pie and happily resting his head on a soft cushion, declared in a sleepy rumble that this was the best shortcut ever. Elio, with a happy sigh and Sparkle glowing softly on his neck, took another slice. The bells in the pinewood kept chiming. The pie tin was almost empty. Nobody asked which path had been fastest.
characters: Elio (young elf who visits Grandmother Elara), Wizard Fizzwick (a wizard who loves speed), Sparkle (a glow-worm who lives in a mossy pouch)
